1	# 1,001 Real-World Gen AI Use Cases from Google Cloud Customers
     2	
     3	## Source
     4	
     5	Google Cloud Blog — "1,001 real-world gen AI use cases from the world's leading organizations"  
     6	URL: https://cloud.google.com/transform/101-real-world-generative-ai-use-cases-from-industry-leaders  
     7	Published: April 12, 2024; last updated: October 9, 2025  
     8	Authors: Matt Renner (President & CRO, Google Cloud), Matt A.V. Chaban (Senior Editor)
     9	
    10	![1,001 AI use cases from Google Cloud customers](./assets/figure_1.jpg)
    11	
    12	## Overview and Growth Trajectory
    13	
    14	Google Cloud first published its list of real-world generative AI use cases during Cloud Next 24 in April 2024, starting with 101 entries. By October 2025, the list had grown **10×** to 1,001 use cases — and the authors note this still only scratches the surface of what is becoming possible.
    15	
    16	The list is organized by **11 major industry groups** and within those, **6 agent types**: Customer, Employee, Creative, Code, Data, and Security. The October 2025 edition added 400 new entries (denoted with an asterisk). Organizations span top companies, governments, researchers, and startups worldwide.
    17	
    18	The 11 industry verticals are:
    19	- Automotive & Logistics
    20	- Business & Professional Services
    21	- Financial Services
    22	- Healthcare & Life Sciences
    23	- Hospitality & Travel
    24	- Manufacturing, Industrial & Electronics
    25	- Media, Marketing & Gaming
    26	- Public Sector & Nonprofits
    27	- Retail
    28	- Technology
    29	- Telecommunications
    30	
    31	## Automotive & Logistics: Detailed Use Cases by Agent Type
    32	
    33	![Automotive & Logistics](./assets/figure_2.jpg)
    34	
    35	The Automotive & Logistics vertical provides one of the richest cross-sections of agent types. Below is a representative sample:
    36	
    37	| Agent Type | Organization | Use Case Summary | Key Metric / Detail |
    38	|---|---|---|---|
    39	| Customer | Mercedes-Benz | MBUX Virtual Assistant powered by Gemini via Vertex AI enables natural driver conversations for navigation and POI | Natural language in-car assistant |
    40	| Customer | LUXGEN (Taiwan EV) | AI agent on LINE answers customer questions via Vertex AI | Reduced human CS workload by **30%** |
    41	| Customer | General Motors (OnStar) | Virtual assistant with Google Cloud conversational AI recognizes speaker intent | Improved intent recognition |
    42	| Customer | Volkswagen of America | myVW app virtual assistant lets drivers query owner's manuals; multimodal camera feature for dashboard indicators | Gemini multimodal capabilities |
    43	| Customer | UPS Capital | DeliveryDefense Address Confidence uses ML to score delivery success likelihood | Data-driven delivery confidence |
    44	| Customer | PODS / Tombras | "World's Smartest Billboard" on trucks adapted to NYC neighborhoods in real time using Gemini | **6,000+ unique headlines**, 299 neighborhoods, 29 hours |
    45	| Employee | Toyota | AI platform on Google Cloud enables factory workers to build and deploy ML models | **10,000+ man-hours/year** saved |
    46	| Employee | Uber | AI agents summarize CS communications and surface prior interaction context | Improved CS rep effectiveness |
    47	| Employee | Rivian | Gemini in Google Workspace for instant research, accelerated learning, and rapid skill acquisition | Faster onboarding and deep research |
    48	| Employee | Rivian | NotebookLM centralizes FAQ answers with verified sources and interactive chat | Reduced repetitive inquiries |
    49	| Employee | Geotab | Google Workspace with Gemini for research, summarization, legal review, data filtering across 4.7M connected vehicles | Cross-functional productivity |
    50	| Employee | Routematic | Migrated entire infrastructure to Google Cloud (Compute Engine, GKE) in 8 months with zero downtime | Release cycles shortened from **weeks to days** |
    51	| Employee | 704 Apps | Gemini analyzes in-trip audio to measure emotional "temperature" and flag hostile language for safety alerts | Real-time safety monitoring |
    52	| Code | Renault Group (Ampere) | Enterprise Gemini Code Assist understands company code base, standards, and conventions | Developer productivity for EV software |
    53	
    54	## Headline ROI and Impact Numbers Across Industries
    55	
    56	Several organizations reported quantified business outcomes:
    57	
    58	- **Mercari** (Japan's largest online marketplace): Anticipates **500% ROI** while reducing employee workloads by **20%** through AI-powered customer service.
    59	- **LUXGEN**: Customer service agent workload reduced by **30%** with Vertex AI chatbot.
    60	- **Toyota**: Factory AI platform saved over **10,000 man-hours per year**.
    61	- **PODS / Tombras**: Generated **6,000+ unique ad headlines** across all 299 NYC neighborhoods in just **29 hours**.
    62	- **Virgin Voyages**: Uses Veo text-to-video to create **thousands of hyper-personalized ads and emails** in a single batch without sacrificing brand voice.
    63	- **Figma**: Enables organizations to create high-quality, brand-approved images and assets **in seconds**.
    64	- **Commerzbank**: Making it easier than ever to reach a customer service agent via gen AI.
    65	
    66	## Cross-Industry Patterns
    67	
    68	Three dominant patterns emerge across the 1,001 use cases:
    69	
    70	1. **Conversational Customer Agents** are the most visible entry point — automotive (Mercedes-Benz, GM, VW, LUXGEN), financial services (Commerzbank), and retail (Mercari) all deploy AI-powered virtual assistants to handle customer queries, reduce wait times, and lower human agent workloads.
    71	
    72	2. **Employee Productivity Agents** are the broadest category — companies like Uber, Rivian, Geotab, and Oxa use Gemini for Google Workspace to summarize documents, accelerate research, draft content, review legal documents, and filter data across departments from HR to engineering.
    73	
    74	3. **Creative and Scale Agents** represent the fastest-growing frontier — Virgin Voyages' hyper-personalized video campaigns, PODS' real-time adaptive billboards, and Figma's instant brand-approved asset generation demonstrate that gen AI is moving from text into multimodal creative production at enterprise scale.
    75	
    76	## Key Findings
    77	
    78	- **10× growth in 18 months**: The list expanded from 101 to 1,001 use cases between April 2024 and October 2025, reflecting accelerating enterprise gen AI adoption.
    79	- **Customer and Employee agents dominate**: Conversational assistants and workplace productivity tools are the most common deployment patterns across all 11 industries.
    80	- **Measurable ROI is being achieved in production**: Organizations report outcomes including 500% ROI (Mercari), 30% workload reduction (LUXGEN), 10,000+ man-hours saved annually (Toyota), and thousands of creative assets generated in hours (Virgin Voyages, PODS).
    81	- **Six agent types provide a useful adoption framework**: Customer, Employee, Creative, Code, Data, and Security agents offer enterprises a structured way to identify and prioritize gen AI opportunities.
    82	- **The pace is accelerating**: With 400 new entries added in the latest update alone, the trajectory suggests enterprise gen AI deployment is still in its early exponential phase.

    51	
    52	# PPTX Manipulation Skill
    53	
    54	## Overview
    55	
    56	This skill enables programmatic creation, editing, and manipulation of Microsoft PowerPoint (.pptx) presentations using the **python-pptx** library. Create professional slides with text, shapes, images, charts, and tables without manual editing.
    57	
    58	## How to Use
    59	
    60	1. Describe the presentation you want to create or modify
    61	2. Provide content, data, or images to include
    62	3. I'll generate python-pptx code and execute it
    63	
    64	**Example prompts:**
    65	- "Create a 10-slide pitch deck from this outline"
    66	- "Add a chart to slide 3 with this data"
    67	- "Extract all text from this presentation"
    68	- "Generate slides from this markdown content"
    69	
    70	## Domain Knowledge
    71	
    72	### python-pptx Fundamentals
    73	
    74	```python
    75	from pptx import Presentation
    76	from pptx.util import Inches, Pt
    77	from pptx.enum.shapes import MSO_SHAPE
    78	from pptx.enum.text import PP_ALIGN
    79	
    80	# Create new presentation
    81	prs = Presentation()
    82	
    83	# Or open existing
    84	prs = Presentation('existing.pptx')
    85	```
    86	
    87	### Presentation Structure
    88	```
    89	Presentation
    90	├── slide_layouts (predefined layouts)
    91	├── slides (individual slides)
    92	│   ├── shapes (text, images, charts)
    93	│   │   ├── text_frame (paragraphs)
    94	│   │   └── table (rows, cells)
    95	│   └── placeholders (title, content)
    96	└── slide_masters (templates)
    97	```
    98	
    99	### Slide Layouts
   100	```python
   101	# Common layout indices (may vary by template)
   102	TITLE_SLIDE = 0
   103	TITLE_CONTENT = 1
   104	SECTION_HEADER = 2
   105	TWO_CONTENT = 3
   106	COMPARISON = 4
   107	TITLE_ONLY = 5
   108	BLANK = 6
   109	
   110	# Add slide with layout
   111	slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[TITLE_CONTENT]
   112	slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
   113	```
   114	
   115	### Adding Content
   116	
   117	#### Title Slide
   118	```python
   119	slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[0]  # Title slide
   120	slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
   121	
   122	title = slide.shapes.title
   123	subtitle = slide.placeholders[1]
   124	
   125	title.text = "Quarterly Report"
   126	subtitle.text = "Q4 2024 Performance Review"
   127	```
   128	
   129	#### Text Content
   130	```python
   131	# Using placeholder
   132	body = slide.placeholders[1]
   133	tf = body.text_frame
   134	tf.text = "First bullet point"
   135	
   136	# Add more paragraphs
   137	p = tf.add_paragraph()
   138	p.text = "Second bullet point"
   139	p.level = 0
   140	
   141	p = tf.add_paragraph()
   142	p.text = "Sub-bullet"
   143	p.level = 1
   144	```
   145	
   146	#### Text Box
   147	```python
   148	from pptx.util import Inches, Pt
   149	
   150	left = Inches(1)
   151	top = Inches(2)
   152	width = Inches(4)
   153	height = Inches(1)
   154	
   155	txBox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(left, top, width, height)
   156	tf = txBox.text_frame
   157	
   158	p = tf.paragraphs[0]
   159	p.text = "Custom text box"
   160	p.font.bold = True
   161	p.font.size = Pt(18)
   162	```
   163	
   164	#### Shapes
   165	```python
   166	from pptx.enum.shapes import MSO_SHAPE
   167	
   168	# Rectangle
   169	shape = slide.shapes.add_shape(
   170	    MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE,
   171	    Inches(1), Inches(2),  # left, top
   172	    Inches(3), Inches(1.5) # width, height
   173	)
   174	shape.text = "Rectangle with text"
   175	
   176	# Common shapes:
   177	# MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, ROUNDED_RECTANGLE
   178	# MSO_SHAPE.OVAL, CHEVRON, ARROW_RIGHT
   179	# MSO_SHAPE.CALLOUT_ROUNDED_RECTANGLE
   180	```
   181	
   182	#### Images
   183	```python
   184	# Add image
   185	slide.shapes.add_picture(
   186	    'image.png',
   187	    Inches(1), Inches(2),  # position
   188	    width=Inches(4)        # auto height
   189	)
   190	
   191	# Or specify both dimensions
   192	slide.shapes.add_picture(
   193	    'logo.png',
   194	    Inches(8), Inches(0.5),
   195	    Inches(1.5), Inches(0.75)
   196	)
   197	```
   198	
   199	### Tables
   200	```python
   201	# Create table
   202	rows, cols = 4, 3
   203	left = Inches(1)
   204	top = Inches(2)
   205	width = Inches(8)
   206	height = Inches(2)
   207	
   208	table = slide.shapes.add_table(rows, cols, left, top, width, height).table
   209	
   210	# Set column widths
   211	table.columns[0].width = Inches(2)
   212	table.columns[1].width = Inches(3)
   213	table.columns[2].width = Inches(3)
   214	
   215	# Add headers
   216	headers = ['Product', 'Q3 Sales', 'Q4 Sales']
   217	for i, header in enumerate(headers):
   218	    cell = table.cell(0, i)
   219	    cell.text = header
   220	    cell.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.bold = True
   221	
   222	# Add data
   223	data = [
   224	    ['Widget A', '$10,000', '$12,500'],
   225	    ['Widget B', '$8,000', '$9,200'],
   226	    ['Widget C', '$15,000', '$18,000'],
   227	]
   228	for row_idx, row_data in enumerate(data, 1):
   229	    for col_idx, value in enumerate(row_data):
   230	        table.cell(row_idx, col_idx).text = value
   231	```
   232	
   233	### Charts
   234	```python
   235	from pptx.chart.data import CategoryChartData
   236	from pptx.enum.chart import XL_CHART_TYPE
   237	
   238	# Chart data
   239	chart_data = CategoryChartData()
   240	chart_data.categories = ['Q1', 'Q2', 'Q3', 'Q4']
   241	chart_data.add_series('Sales', (19.2, 21.4, 16.7, 23.8))
   242	chart_data.add_series('Expenses', (12.1, 15.3, 14.2, 18.1))
   243	
   244	# Add chart
   245	x, y, cx, cy = Inches(1), Inches(2), Inches(8), Inches(4)
   246	chart = slide.shapes.add_chart(
   247	    XL_CHART_TYPE.COLUMN_CLUSTERED,
   248	    x, y, cx, cy, chart_data
   249	).chart
   250	
   251	# Customize
   252	chart.has_legend = True
   253	chart.legend.include_in_layout = False
   254	```
   255	
   256	### Formatting
   257	
   258	#### Text Formatting
   259	```python
   260	from pptx.dml.color import RGBColor
   261	
   262	run = p.runs[0]
   263	run.font.name = 'Arial'
   264	run.font.size = Pt(24)
   265	run.font.bold = True
   266	run.font.italic = True
   267	run.font.color.rgb = RGBColor(0x00, 0x66, 0xCC)
   268	```
   269	
   270	#### Shape Fill & Line
   271	```python
   272	from pptx.dml.color import RGBColor
   273	
   274	shape.fill.solid()
   275	shape.fill.fore_color.rgb = RGBColor(0x00, 0x80, 0x00)
   276	
   277	shape.line.color.rgb = RGBColor(0x00, 0x00, 0x00)
   278	shape.line.width = Pt(2)
   279	```
   280	
   281	#### Paragraph Alignment
   282	```python
   283	from pptx.enum.text import PP_ALIGN
   284	
   285	p.alignment = PP_ALIGN.CENTER  # LEFT, RIGHT, JUSTIFY
   286	```
   287	
   288	## Best Practices
   289	
   290	1. **Use Templates**: Start with a .pptx template for consistent branding
   291	2. **Layout First**: Plan slide structure before coding
   292	3. **Reuse Slide Masters**: Maintain consistency across presentations
   293	4. **Optimize Images**: Compress images before adding
   294	5. **Test Output**: Always verify generated presentations
   295	
   296	## Common Patterns
   297	
   298	### Slide Deck Generator
   299	```python
   300	def create_deck(title, slides_content):
   301	    prs = Presentation()
   302	    
   303	    # Title slide
   304	    slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[0])
   305	    slide.shapes.title.text = title
   306	    
   307	    # Content slides
   308	    for slide_data in slides_content:
   309	        slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[1])
   310	        slide.shapes.title.text = slide_data['title']
   311	        
   312	        body = slide.placeholders[1]
   313	        tf = body.text_frame
   314	        for i, point in enumerate(slide_data['points']):
   315	            if i == 0:
   316	                tf.text = point
   317	            else:
   318	                p = tf.add_paragraph()
   319	                p.text = point
   320	    
   321	    return prs
   322	```
   323	
   324	### Data-Driven Charts
   325	```python
   326	def add_bar_chart(slide, title, categories, values):
   327	    from pptx.chart.data import CategoryChartData
   328	    from pptx.enum.chart import XL_CHART_TYPE
   329	    
   330	    chart_data = CategoryChartData()
   331	    chart_data.categories = categories
   332	    chart_data.add_series('Values', values)
   333	    
   334	    chart = slide.shapes.add_chart(
   335	        XL_CHART_TYPE.BAR_CLUSTERED,
   336	        Inches(1), Inches(2),
   337	        Inches(8), Inches(4),
   338	        chart_data
   339	    ).chart
   340	    
   341	    chart.chart_title.text_frame.text = title
   342	    return chart
   343	```
   344	
   345	## Examples
   346	
   347	### Example 1: Create a Pitch Deck
   348	```python
   349	from pptx import Presentation
   350	from pptx.util import Inches, Pt
   351	
   352	prs = Presentation()
   353	
   354	# Slide 1: Title
   355	slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[0])
   356	slide.shapes.title.text = "StartupX"
   357	slide.placeholders[1].text = "Revolutionizing Document Processing"
   358	
   359	# Slide 2: Problem
   360	slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[1])
   361	slide.shapes.title.text = "The Problem"
   362	body = slide.placeholders[1].text_frame
   363	body.text = "Manual document processing costs businesses $1T annually"
   364	p = body.add_paragraph()
   365	p.text = "Average worker spends 20% of time on document tasks"
   366	p.level = 1
   367	
   368	# Slide 3: Solution
   369	slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[1])
   370	slide.shapes.title.text = "Our Solution"
   371	body = slide.placeholders[1].text_frame
   372	body.text = "AI-powered document automation"
   373	body.add_paragraph().text = "90% faster processing"
   374	body.add_paragraph().text = "99.5% accuracy"
   375	body.add_paragraph().text = "Works with existing tools"
   376	
   377	# Slide 4: Market
   378	slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[5])  # Title only
   379	slide.shapes.title.text = "Market Opportunity: $50B by 2028"
   380	
   381	# Add chart
   382	from pptx.chart.data import CategoryChartData
   383	from pptx.enum.chart import XL_CHART_TYPE
   384	
   385	data = CategoryChartData()
   386	data.categories = ['2024', '2025', '2026', '2027', '2028']
   387	data.add_series('Market Size ($B)', [30, 35, 40, 45, 50])
   388	
   389	slide.shapes.add_chart(
   390	    XL_CHART_TYPE.LINE,
   391	    Inches(1), Inches(1.5),
   392	    Inches(8), Inches(5),
   393	    data
   394	)
   395	
   396	prs.save('pitch_deck.pptx')
   397	```
   398	
   399	### Example 2: Report with Data Table
   400	```python
   401	from pptx import Presentation
   402	from pptx.util import Inches, Pt
   403	
   404	prs = Presentation()
   405

COLOR_MID_GRAY = RGBColor(0x88, 0x88, 0x88)

# ── Helper utilities ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def set_slide_bg(slide, color):
    """Set solid background color for a slide."""
    background = slide.background
    fill = background.fill
    fill.solid()
    fill.fore_color.rgb = color

def add_textbox(slide, left, top, width, height, text, font_size=Pt(14),
                font_color=COLOR_TEXT, bold=False, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT,
                font_name="Segoe UI", italic=False, word_wrap=True):
    """Add a text box with full formatting control."""
    txBox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(left, top, width, height)
    tf = txBox.text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = word_wrap
    p = tf.paragraphs[0]
    p.text = text
    p.font.size = font_size
    p.font.color.rgb = font_color
    p.font.bold = bold
    p.font.italic = italic
    p.font.name = font_name
    p.alignment = align
    return txBox

def add_rounded_rect(slide, left, top, width, height, fill_color, line_color=None, line_width=Pt(1)):
    shape = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.ROUNDED_RECTANGLE, left, top, width, height)
    shape.fill.solid()
    shape.fill.fore_color.rgb = fill_color
    if line_color:
        shape.line.color.rgb = line_color
        shape.line.width = line_width
    else:
        shape.line.fill.background()
    return shape

def add_bullet_list(slide, left, top, width, height, items, font_size=Pt(16),
                    font_color=COLOR_TEXT, bullet_color=COLOR_ACCENT,
                    font_name="Segoe UI", line_spacing=1.3):
    txBox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(left, top, width, height)
    tf = txBox.text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    for i, item in enumerate(items):
        if i == 0:
            p = tf.paragraphs[0]
        else:
            p = tf.add_paragraph()
        p.text = item
        p.font.size = font_size
        p.font.color.rgb = font_color
        p.font.name = font_name
        p.space_after = Pt(12)
        p.level = 0
    return txBox

    add_textbox(slide, x + Inches(0.35), y + Inches(1.25), card_w - Inches(0.5), Inches(1.2),
                desc, font_size=Pt(12), font_color=COLOR_TEXT, bold=False,
                align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT, font_name="Segoe UI")

# Footer note
add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(6.7), Inches(12), Inches(0.4),
            "These are production-deployed outcomes, not pilot results.  Source: Google Cloud customer reports, October 2025.",
            font_size=Pt(12), font_color=COLOR_MID_GRAY, bold=False,
            align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT, font_name="Segoe UI")

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# SLIDE 6 — Cross-Industry Patterns (3-column layout)
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6])
set_slide_bg(slide, COLOR_WHITE)

# Title
add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(0.35), Inches(12), Inches(0.7),
            "Common Patterns: Customer Assistants, Employee Productivity, and Creative Scale",
            font_size=Pt(30), font_color=COLOR_DARK, bold=True,
            align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT, font_name="Segoe UI")

ul = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, Inches(0.6), Inches(0.95), Inches(1.5), Inches(0.06))
ul.fill.solid()
ul.fill.fore_color.rgb = COLOR_ACCENT
ul.line.fill.background()

patterns = [
    (
        "Conversational Customer Agents",
        COLOR_ACCENT,
        "The most visible entry point across industries.",
        [
            "Automotive: Mercedes-Benz MBUX, GM OnStar, VW myVW, LUXGEN chatbot",
            "Financial Services: Commerzbank gen AI customer service routing",
            "Retail: Mercari AI-powered customer service",
            "Outcome: reduced wait times, lower human agent workloads, 24/7 availability"
        ]
    ),
    (
        "Employee Productivity Agents",
        COLOR_ACCENT2,
        "The broadest category — spanning every department.",
        [
            "Uber: AI agents summarize CS communications and surface context",
            "Rivian: Gemini in Workspace for research, onboarding, and NotebookLM FAQs",
            "Geotab: Cross-functional productivity across 4.7M connected vehicles",
            "Outcome: faster research, automated drafting, reduced repetitive inquiries"
        ]
    ),
    (
        "Creative and Scale Agents",
        COLOR_ACCENT3,
        "The fastest-growing frontier — multimodal creative production.",
        [
            "Virgin Voyages: Veo text-to-video for thousands of hyper-personalized ads",
            "PODS / Tombras: 6,000+ unique headlines across 299 NYC neighborhoods in 29 hours",
            "Figma: high-quality, brand-approved images and assets in seconds",
            "Outcome: mass personalization without sacrificing brand voice"
        ]
    ),
]

col_w = Inches(4.0)
start_x = Inches(0.5)
start_y = Inches(1.25)
for idx, (title, color, subtitle, bullets) in enumerate(patterns):
    x = start_x + idx * (col_w + Inches(0.15))
    
    # Card background
    card = add_rounded_rect(slide, x, start_y, col_w, Inches(5.1), COLOR_WHITE,
                            line_color=RGBColor(0xE0, 0xE0, 0xE0), line_width=Pt(1))
    
    # Top color bar
    top_bar = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, x, start_y, col_w, Inches(0.12))
    top_bar.fill.solid()
    top_bar.fill.fore_color.rgb = color
    top_bar.line.fill.background()
    
    add_textbox(slide, x + Inches(0.2), start_y + Inches(0.3), col_w - Inches(0.4), Inches(0.5),
                title, font_size=Pt(17), font_color=color, bold=True,
                align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT, font_name="Segoe UI")
    add_textbox(slide, x + Inches(0.2), start_y + Inches(0.8), col_w - Inches(0.4), Inches(0.35),
                subtitle, font_size=Pt(12), font_color=COLOR_MID_GRAY, bold=False,
                align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT, font_name="Segoe UI")
    
    # Bullets
    txBox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(x + Inches(0.2), start_y + Inches(1.2), col_w - Inches(0.4), Inches(3.6))
    tf = txBox.text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    for i, b in enumerate(bullets):
        if i == 0:
            p = tf.paragraphs[0]
        else:
            p = tf.add_paragraph()
        p.text = "•  " + b
        p.font.size = Pt(12)
        p.font.color.rgb = COLOR_TEXT
        p.font.name = "Segoe UI"
        p.space_after = Pt(10)

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# SLIDE 7 — Strategic Takeaways
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6])
set_slide_bg(slide, COLOR_DARK)

# Accent bar
bar = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, Inches(0), Inches(0), SLIDE_WIDTH, Inches(0.15))
bar.fill.solid()
bar.fill.fore_color.rgb = COLOR_ACCENT
bar.line.fill.background()

# Title
add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(0.5), Inches(12), Inches(0.7),
            "Takeaways: Where to Start and What to Expect from Enterprise Gen AI",
            font_size=Pt(32), font_color=COLOR_WHITE, bold=True,
            align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT, font_name="Segoe UI")

ul = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, Inches(0.6), Inches(1.15), Inches(1.5), Inches(0.06))
ul.fill.solid()
ul.fill.fore_color.rgb = COLOR_ACCENT
ul.line.fill.background()

takeaways = [
    ("1", "Gen AI is production-ready across all major industries",
     "1,001 use cases spanning 11 verticals prove the technology has moved well beyond pilots into live production systems."),
    ("2", "Customer and Employee agents are the most common entry points",
     "Conversational assistants and workplace productivity tools offer the fastest path to measurable ROI with lowest risk."),
    ("3", "Measurable ROI is achievable within months",
     "Organizations report 500% ROI (Mercari), 30% workload reduction (LUXGEN), and 10,000+ hours saved annually (Toyota)."),
    ("4", "Creative and Code agents are emerging fast",
     "Virgin Voyages, PODS, and Figma demonstrate that multimodal creative production and developer acceleration are the next frontiers."),
    ("5", "The pace of adoption is accelerating — early movers gain compounding advantages",
     "400 new entries in the latest update alone; 10× growth in 18 months signals we are still in the early exponential phase."),
]

start_y = Inches(1.5)
for idx, (num, title, desc) in enumerate(takeaways):
    y = start_y + idx * Inches(1.05)
    
    # Number circle
    circ = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.OVAL, Inches(0.6), y + Pt(2), Inches(0.45), Inches(0.45))
    circ.fill.solid()
    circ.fill.fore_color.rgb = COLOR_ACCENT
    circ.line.fill.background()
    add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.6), y + Pt(6), Inches(0.45), Inches(0.35),
                num, font_size=Pt(16), font_color=COLOR_WHITE, bold=True,
                align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER, font_name="Segoe UI")
    
    add_textbox(slide, Inches(1.2), y, Inches(11.5), Inches(0.35),
                title, font_size=Pt(18), font_color=COLOR_WHITE, bold=True,
                align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT, font_name="Segoe UI")
    add_textbox(slide, Inches(1.2), y + Inches(0.32), Inches(11.5), Inches(0.5),
                desc, font_size=Pt(13), font_color=COLOR_LIGHT_GRAY, bold=False,
                align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT, font_name="Segoe UI")

# Source footer
add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(6.7), Inches(12), Inches(0.4),
            "Source: Google Cloud — '1,001 real-world gen AI use cases from the world's leading organizations' (October 2025)",
            font_size=Pt(11), font_color=COLOR_MID_GRAY, bold=False,
            align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT, font_name="Segoe UI")

# ── Save ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
prs.save('/app/output/final_deck.pptx')
print("Presentation saved to /app/output/final_deck.pptx")
